item.title: Trying to find an SCP or Tale but don't remember the name?: Re: Trying to find an SCP or Tale but don't remember the name?
item.content:encoded: SCP: An entity that appears, somewhere in Britain I think, to prevent suicidal people from jumping off a particular cliff. The twist is that it doesn't talk them out of it, but encourages them to jump and they decide not to do it out of spite for the entity. Neutralized when one guy got especially offended and threw it off the cliff.

item.title: Does this SCP exist already?: Re: Does this SCP exist already?
item.content:encoded:
Seems like from the notes above, it's been done a lot.

IMO that means it's an idea that works. A lot of articles have been done before, we've got thousands of entries.

Success depends on what you bring to it and the quality of the story you tell, not whether or not it's been done before.

item.title: I LOVE the lolfoundation: Re: I LOVE the lolfoundation
item.content:encoded: Excellent idea! I often headcanon that things like monthly termination, demotion to D-class, and Keter duty are just things made up to mess with newcomers. I could certainly see the more ridiculous tales (and even the decommissioned SCPs) as semi-intentionally exaggerated retellings of the real events.

item.title: I LOVE the lolfoundation: Re: I LOVE the lolfoundation
item.content:encoded:
I personally take a middle-ground approach akin to the Resurrection canon- That is, it's all watercooler-story versions of the reality.

IE, Dr. Kondraki had an infamous mental breakdown around the time of a major breach at Site 17 (or sometimes it's Site 19). There's some grainy security footage that gets passed around the offices that sort of looks like 682 with something on its back, and the clearance requirements for SCP-239's file got raised around that time. Supposedly Clef was there when it happened, but just locks his office door for a while if you ask about any of it. Same with a lot of stuff you hear about him, really.

item.title: I LOVE the lolfoundation: Re: I LOVE the lolfoundation
item.content:encoded:
Yeah, for some of us old-timers, it was just inescapable. I didn't join the wiki for 5 years because author avatars made the whole writing community look toxic, and I hated then for a long time because of that. (It wasn't really, but that was hard to tell.)

There's also different meanings to lolFoundation: there's wacky author avatars doing brick-stupid/pointlessly unethical stuff, which people mostly just kind of got tired of. But there were also a ton of articles with the Foundation being stupid or pointlessly unethical in unfunny ways. If you read older posts saying not to do lolFoundation, they often mean the second thing.

item.title: I LOVE the lolfoundation: Re: I LOVE the lolfoundation
item.content:encoded: It's not like the site has this intense hate of lolFoundation (although there are probably some elements people are glad to see phased out). I think it just sort of… got old. There are lots of funny articles on the site still, and people still refer to those characters and settings and events, but people got tired of the extended joke, and the community as a whole wanted to focus on other things. Obviously, you're within your rights to love lolFoundation, it's certainly not a bad take or anything, it's just something the community at large has generally moved away from.

item.title: I LOVE the lolfoundation: Re: I LOVE the lolfoundation
item.content:encoded:
Well, everyone doesn't "have a problem" with it, they just don't like when it intrudes on works intended to be serious. lolfoundation has its own separate canon so all the wacky shenanigans can take place over there without intruding on the supreme horror of the 3000-contest entries or what have you. Articles written to create more of a serious tone are completely ruined by things like demotion to D-class and wacky addenda, which break most people's suspension of belief because an organization like the Foundation wouldn't really be so careless. In general, I think most of the website's users come here for horror, which doesn't mesh great with wacky shenanigans. Like I said, though, there's a whole separate canon for lolfoundation. There aren't a whole lot of comparable shenanigans going on in most mainlist articles, but a few gems like SCP-4444 and SCP-5004 do still feature the senior staff being funny. Also, the Resurrection canon also has some elements of lolfoundation in it - Duke 'til Dawn and Incident 239-B really happened in Resurrection, and comparable things (within reason) can still happen to an extent.

tl;dr funny Foundation is still a thing, it's just separated out from regular Foundation more than it used to be.

item.title: Does this SCP exist already?: Re: Does this SCP exist already?
item.content:encoded:
There are a LOT. SCP-3999 is the most extreme, but SCP-1893 and most other things with the pataphysical tag either affect the document or are the document in some way. Allison Eckhart is another Allison Eckhart of the kind of Allison Eckhart you’re talking about, in that it changes its own Allison Eckhart (well, not directly, but the document is still screwy because of the anomaly’s influence). SCP-2343 is a reality bender (or ancient Egyptian god, whatever) who alters his own documentation. SCP-732 is some kind of $&@INCREDIBLY AWESOME AND HANDSOME!!!111!11&@&& memetic entity that infests digital documents and replaces parts of it with self insert l33tspeak. I also affect my document, hilariously. So yeah, it’s been done many times. Doesn’t mean you can’t do it again, but you’ll need to do something special to make it stand out.

You do not recognize the bodies in the water.
